words.d: the flat metal tray you bake food on in the oven
the machine whose blades mix food into a drink
to push soft food over a surface in a thin layer
to let frozen food become soft again
the bright burning part of a fire or candle
a plant like basil used to flavour food
a device for weighing things
a strong-tasting powder used to flavour food
to heat food in a microwave oven
to taste a little of something
the act of burning something
a state of extreme ruin and misfortune
a flour mixture you can knead or roll
a fast military plane that fights enemy aircraft
any material that fills a space or container
to bend so that one part covers the other
to act in the way rules tell you
to make something hot or hotter
made at home by yourself, not bought
a substance of two or more things mixed together
a dish baked in pastry
making two sides equal
to have people expecting a lot from you
formal approval given to something
covered in red, like from a wound
to make a meal from raw ingredients
to chop something into many small pieces
a protein that makes a chemical change happen
the soft white grease in meat
the soft meat under an animal's skin
a flat metal dish with a long handle
green leafy vegetables you eat
to watch carefully so nothing goes wrong
to put things one on top of another
the deep dish that sits under a food mixer

to cook food so it is ready to eat

videos.desc: In a log-cabin kitchen a woman shows a black baking sheet, lines it with parchment, arranges potatoes, peppers and carrots in one layer, oils them and slides the sheet into the oven; later the couple pulls out the roasted vegetables and the man tastes one.
videos.said: one layer always golden listen to it it's

videos.desc: A retro-cartoon man in a green tracksuit drops strawberries, a banana and milk into a blender, blends it into a pink smoothie, opens the lid and gets a blob of smoothie on his nose, tastes it, then pours the drink into a glass and gives a thumbs up.

A 3D-animated girl saws a slab off an enormous block of butter and drags it across a slice of bread with a knife until the whole surface is covered in a glossy layer, then bites into it with her eyes closed in bliss.

A cartoon man takes a rock-hard frozen fish out of the freezer and thunks it on the counter, then fills a bowl with water in the sink and soaks the fish until he can proudly hold up the floppy, defrosted fillet.
A couple picks fresh basil leaves from little potted plants on a windowsill by the sea, pinches and rubs them to smell the aroma, then scatters the leaves over a plate of spaghetti with tomato sauce.
videos.said: Pinch rub smell Just a few leaves

videos.desc: A young couple in a rustic kitchen weighs ingredients on a vintage kitchen scale, placing a bowl on it and pouring flour in while watching the dial. Then their tabby cat jumps onto the scale and sits on it, and they laugh.
videos.said: Climbing. Climbing. Stop! Your turn apparently.

videos.desc: At a night souk, a vendor scoops bright red spice powder from tall colored mounds into a paper cone; a couple sniffs it and the man's eyes go wide at how strong it is. At home they sprinkle the spice into a hot pan of oil, where it blooms into a red star, then cook peppers in it and taste the dish.
videos.said: Wow, that's strong! Look at the color!

videos.desc: In an anime kitchen at night, a green-haired boy puts a bowl of noodles into a microwave, starts it and watches the bowl spin and steam; he pulls the hot bowl out with an "ow, hot, hot!", puts on oven mitts, and a girl points at the microwave asking for hers next.
videos.said: Ow! Hot, hot! My next please.

videos.desc: A hand lowers two slices of white bread into slots on the back of a grey model fighter jet standing on a granite kitchen counter. The heating elements inside the slots glow orange and a blue-and-orange flame roars out of the jet's exhaust nozzle like an afterburner. The flame dies down and the hand lifts out two browned slices.

A hand drops two slices of bread into slots on the spine of a grey twin-engine model fighter jet parked on a granite kitchen counter. The elements glow orange, then long blue flames shoot from both exhaust nozzles. When the flames cut out, two golden-brown slices stand proud of the slots and the hand reaches in to take them.

A man in a chef's hat carries a big glass bowl of red and green apples through a kitchen, followed by a black and white cow that is also wearing a chef's hat. At the counter he rolls out dough with a rolling pin while the cow watches over his shoulder and licks its nose. He lays overlapping apple slices in a neat circle inside a pastry-lined dish and slides it into the oven. At a wooden table the finished golden pie sits whole beside a glass of milk, and in the last shot the plate holds only crumbs while the man laughs and the cow leans in over the table.

In a rustic kitchen a young woman and an older woman shape pale balls of dough and set them in rows on a baking tray dusted with flour. The older woman opens the oven and they slide the trays of raw dough inside. Later the oven is opened again and trays of golden baked croissants come out steaming, filling the table.

In a rustic kitchen a woman in an embroidered blouse leans over a gas hob where a blue flame burns under a small saucepan. Beside it a big pot of water rolls at a full boil and white steam streams off the surface towards the window. She reaches for a huge lidded pot, lifts the heavy lid, and a thick white cloud of steam bursts up into her face; she rears back with her mouth open.

A young man in a stained apron stands in a small home kitchen while everything he is cooking goes wrong at once. Two slices of toast, black and smoking, pop up in the toaster in the foreground. He turns to a frying pan of vegetables on the gas hob and pushes them around with a spatula, wincing. Smoke drifts across the room. He opens the oven and a cloud of smoke rolls out around a roasting bird; he flaps a blue-striped tea towel at the smoke, coughing, the kitchen hazy behind him.

Evening on a beach, sea and dark headland behind. A woman in a checked shirt sits at a low concrete fire pit holding long skewers of marshmallows over the fire. One marshmallow catches light and burns with a tall orange flame right in front of the camera; she pulls back, laughing and open-mouthed. She lowers the other skewers into the flames, and the fire builds until a column of fire and sparks fills the frame against the dark blue sky.

An older woman in a red cardigan stands at a floured wooden table making dumplings. Her hands close a round wrapper over its filling and press the edge over on itself into a ridge of little pleats, and she sets each finished one down in neat rows on the tray in front of her, dozens of them. Her family gathers round her under a paper lantern and red decorations: a man, a woman and two small children in red, the children copying her hands. At the end the man lifts the lid off a bamboo steamer and steam billows up over a basket of finished dumplings while everyone leans in and laughs.

A marshmallow on a stick chars over a toaster, then a bearded man in a strawberry-print apron turns rows of hot dogs on an outdoor barbecue with tongs. The grill erupts and a wall of orange flame leaps waist-high off the grate; the man keeps turning the sausages while a semicircle of relatives behind him stare open-mouthed.

In a modern kitchen at dusk, a man in a denim shirt with a towel over his shoulder lifts a spoonful of tomato-vegetable soup from a pot on the stove, blows on it and tastes it, then holds the spoon out for the woman beside him, who leans in and tastes it too. She smiles and nods. He then brings a bouquet of flowers out from behind his back; she gasps in delight, and they step onto the balcony and hug in front of the city lights.

In a rustic kitchen with painted pottery on wooden shelves, a young woman in an apron and an older woman in a headscarf stand at a floured wooden table. They push and fold a large pale mass of bread dough with their hands, laughing together, until it is shaped into a smooth round loaf on the flour-dusted table.

In a bright home kitchen a young man in a beanie makes a pancake. A knob of butter melts and slides across a large non-stick pan on the hob. He holds a ladle high over the pan and pours a thick pale batter into it in a steady stream; the batter spreads into a wide circle and bubbles rise on its surface. At the end he lifts the pan off the hob and tilts it towards the camera to show the browned pancake.

In a sunny kitchen a young woman in an apron and a green headscarf works through a handwritten page step by step. She leans over it and points at a line, chops cherry tomatoes on a board, tips them into a big bowl of cut vegetables, holds the page up and reads the next step, pours olive oil over the salad, then lays the page flat on the worktop and smiles at the finished bowl.

A woman in a red embroidered apron makes dumplings on a big wooden table in a log kitchen. A white bowl of dark red fruit filling stands at her elbow next to a lump of dough and a row of flat dough circles; she takes each circle, closes it around a spoonful of the filling and presses the edge shut, laying the finished half-moons out in rows across the table. She carries a full board of them to a wide black pan of boiling water over an open fire while a small boy in an embroidered shirt watches, tastes one from a spoon over the steaming pan, and finally sets a wooden bowl of cooked dumplings on the table beside the bowl of red filling.

In a bakery with dark green tiles, shelves of round loaves and a glowing brass oven, a smiling young man in a white t-shirt and grey apron sprinkles flour into the left pan of a tall brass beam balance, while the right pan holds a small brass weight. He then lowers his hand and watches as the two pans hang almost level. The balance stands on a marble counter beside a linen sack and bowls. A brass lamp hangs above, and a golden puppy sleeps on the speckled floor below.

In a grand gilded hall with a painted ceiling and a huge crystal chandelier, a young chef in a white jacket, her hair in a bun, stands behind a table with a white cloth and carefully adds a piece to a tall pink and gold cake built from sugar shards. Three judges lean in close to inspect it: a woman in a burgundy blazer, a young man in a navy suit who straightens up with a serious look, and a woman in a green dress. A trolley stands on the patterned parquet floor.

In a busy restaurant kitchen, a young head chef in a white jacket tastes a spoonful from a plate of seared scallops on yellow purée and gives an approving smile. Beside him a young cook in a navy apron pumps both fists in the air and laughs with relief. The chef lowers the spoon, smiles at the plate and slides it toward the cook, who claps his hands together, beaming. Copper pans hang on a rail, green pendant lamps light cream tiles, and other cooks work in the background.

In a restaurant kitchen, a blender full of red tomato sauce bursts and sprays a young man in a white vest and a cream apron. He throws up his hands in shock, wipes his face and then stands still at the counter, his face, shoulder and arm dripping with bright red sauce, looking fed up. Red splashes cover the white tiles and the steel counter. A young woman in a black top and apron stands behind him, smiling and holding the blender's clear lid. Jars of spices sit on a shelf above.

At a lakeside campsite at dusk with string lights between the pines, a young man in a black vest and a beige apron throws a bunch of fresh homemade noodles into the air in a cloud of flour. He catches them, stretches the long noodles wide between his hands and lays them on a wooden board. On the folding table are flour, eggs and eggshells, tomatoes, garlic and spring onions, and a pot steams on a camping stove. Friends with takeaway boxes watch amazed, and a dog looks up.

At a street party at sunset, a young man with dark hair in a white T-shirt and a flour-dusted apron leans over a long wooden table and runs a pizza cutter through a huge rectangular pizza, cutting it into neat square pieces. Hands reach in, and a woman in a yellow raincoat and a man in a blue cap take slices onto plates. Behind them a man clutches his head, and a brass band plays under strings of colourful bunting between market stalls.

Inside a small cheese dairy with stone floors, a young woman in a white cap, white jacket and blue apron holds a fresh block of white curd over a large copper vat while whey drips back into the yellowish liquid below. In her other hand she holds a tiny measuring spoon. She looks at the curd, smiles and lowers it back into the liquid. Wooden cheese moulds are stacked on the left, shelves of round cheeses stand on the right, and a glass of whey and a cheesecloth lie in front.

On an old gas cooker by a sunny kitchen window, a thick slab of pork belly with a wide white layer of fat sizzles in a black cast-iron pan full of bubbling melted fat. Drops spit into the air, and melted fat runs over the rim of the pan and drips down past the blue flame. A bowl of solid white lard sits beside the stove, and another raw slab of pork belly lies on a wooden board with salt and a cleaver. Wooden spoons stand in a jar against the tiles.

Inside a fish market hall, a young woman with a long blonde braid, a black beanie, a navy jumper and an orange apron stands at a marble counter covered in ice with a whole salmon. In a blue-gloved hand she lifts back the top half of the fish and lays it open, showing thick, bright orange flesh, then smooths it flat. An older man in a green jacket leans on the counter, watching closely, and his eyes widen. Mackerel, prawns and lemons lie on ice in front, and other fishmongers work behind.

At a desert campsite at dusk with pink clouds and red rock buttes behind, a bearded young man in a cream jacket crouches by a campfire and reaches up as a black cast-iron frying pan and a pancake fly high above him. A young woman in a knitted cardigan walks up holding another pan; the pancake drops towards her, and she then lifts her pan high and cheers while he holds his own pan again. Friends sit near white bell tents, beside a table with a bowl of batter and a stack of pancakes, and a dog watches.

A young woman chef with short black hair and hoop earrings, in a white chef's jacket, stands in a busy restaurant kitchen holding a big steel bowl and looking up at fresh leafy greens, kale and spinach leaves flying through the air above her. The leaves fall down into her bowl, and she lowers her eyes and smiles with the bowl full of greens. Behind her two male cooks work at the stoves, steam rises from a pot on the left, copper pans hang overhead and piles of green leaves lie on the steel counter.

A barbecue on a sandy beach at sunset. A young woman in a red bandana, an open blue shirt and a denim apron turns sausages and corn on a round black grill with tongs and glares sideways at a big seagull. The seagull stands on a small wooden table beside her next to a plate of burger buns. She turns to it and points her finger at it in warning. A laughing man in a bucket hat and sunglasses stands behind her. Paper lanterns hang on a string above, and a woman in a yellow swimsuit plays volleyball by the sea.

A village fair on a grey day, under a marquee with bunting. A young man in a white chef's jacket and striped apron stands on a stepladder and pours a thick stream of cream from a big metal pot into a giant glass bowl, adding the top layer to a huge trifle. Through the glass the layers of sponge, fruit, jelly, custard and berries are stacked one above another. He then lifts the empty pot away and smiles. A crowd behind a rope watches and claps, a woman covers her face and a man steadies the ladder.

A sunny country kitchen. A big silver stand mixer whips chocolate batter and cream in its large steel mixing bowl so fast that batter splashes out and flour hangs in the air. A beagle at the counter edge jumps up, catches a flying splash of cream in its mouth and then licks its lips. Broken eggshells and a raw yolk lie on the floury wooden counter with a wooden spoon, a pile of sugar, a kitchen timer and muffins on a cooling rack, an open recipe book stands behind the mixer and copper pans hang on the wall.

Inside a busy old-style Italian restaurant with copper pans hanging from the ceiling, a young woman in a cream silk blouse grips a huge wooden pepper mill with both hands and grinds black pepper onto a plate of pasta on a red checked tablecloth. She straightens up and lifts the mill higher and higher above her head while she keeps grinding. The young man next to her laughs and then hides his face in his hand. A waiter behind them holds another wooden pepper mill and raises his eyebrows. A water carafe and a bread basket stand on the table.

At a busy street food market at night, a young woman in a black vest top, a patterned bandana and a brown apron stands at a steel counter and tosses noodles, prawns and spring onions in a black wok over a gas burner. A tall burst of orange flame and steam shoots up into the dark blue sky, then new flames flare up from the wok as she keeps tossing. Bowls of chopped green onion and red chilli stand in front of her, and a crowd under strings of light bulbs watches behind her.

A bright country kitchen with pale green cupboards, wooden shelves and an open door to the garden. A young man in a white apron and navy T-shirt stands at the stove and laughs as he flips a pancake high into the air from a frying pan, catches it and flips it again; a plate of pancakes sits beside him. At the same time, out in the garden behind him, a golden retriever digs in a raised vegetable bed, throwing out carrots and lettuces, looks up for a moment and keeps digging.
